title: Postnatal persistence of hippocampal Cajal-Retzius cells has a critical role in the establishment of the hippocampal circuit
projectDescription: Cajal-Retzius (CR) cells are a transient neuron type that populate the postnatal hippocampus. The role of transient cell types and circuits have been vastly addressed in neocortical regions, but poorly studied in the hippocampus. To understand how CR cells persistence influences the maturation of hippocampal circuits, we specifically ablated CR cells from the postnatal hippocampus. We observed layer-specific changes in the dendritic complexity and spine density of CA1 pyramidal cells. We were able to identify significant changes in the expression levels of Latrophilin-2, a postsynaptic guidance molecule known for its role in the entorhinal-hippocampal connectivity. Those findings were supported by changes in the overall synaptic proteomic content in CA1 Stratum Lacunosum-Moleculare.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Protein samples were extracted using the Total RNA and Protein Isolation Kit from Macherey- Nagel at postnatal day (P) 15 and P30 from microdissected CA1 Stratum Lacunosum-Moleculare tissue samples of Pde1c-Cre-mice which were previously injected at P0 with AAV-mCherry-flex-DTA to ablate CR-cells. Cre-positive animals form the experimental group and Cre-negative littermates the control group. Protein concentrations were detected using the Protein Quantification assay (Macherey-Nagel) and maximal 1 µg of total protein extract were processed for LC-MS/MS. Tryptic peptide samples were generated by in gel digestion. Protein samples were run for 200 V, 6 min using Invitrogen Bolt Bis-Tris Plus gel with MOPS running buffer (ThermoFisher) and visualized using READYBLUE™ PROTEIN GEL STAIN (SIGMA). The gel-lanes were cut out and proteins were digested using trypsin. The gel pieces were distained using repeatedly 5 min washes with 50 mM NH4HCO3/50% (v/v) CH3CN until visibly coomassie were removed. The gel pieces were dehydrated by adding 500 µL 100% CH3CN until the gel pieces shrinked and became white. The gel pieces were rehydrated using 10 mM DTT in 50 mM NH4HCO3 at 60°C for 30 min. The samples were cooled down to room temperature (RT) and 5 mM iodoacetamide in 50 mM NH4HCO3 were added and incubated in dark for 30 min at RT. After reduction and alkylation, the solution was removed, and the gel pieces again dehydrated as before. Trypsin 12.5 ng/µL in 50 mM NH4HCO3 was added until the gel pieces got rehydrated. Finally, 50 mM NH4HCO3 was added to keep the gel pieces wet during incubation at 37°C over-night. After digestion the samples were dried using a speedvac. Peptides were resuspended in 100 µL 0.1% (v/v) trifluoroacetic acid and desalted using Oasis-HLB 96 well C18 SPE plates. After elution of peptides from C18 the samples were dried in speedvac and further dissolved in 15 µL 0.1% (v/v) formic acid and LC-MS/MS was performed on a timsTOF Pro (Bruker Daltonics) connected to a nanoElute (Bruker Daltonics) HPLC. Peptide separation was done using an Aurora (75 µm × 25 cm) column with running buffers A (0.1% (v/v) formic acid) and B (0.1% (v/v) formic acid in acetonitrile) with a gradient from 0% B to 40% B for 80 min. The timsTOF instrument was operated in the DDA PASEF mode with 10 PASEF scans per acquisition cycle and accumulation and ramp times of 100 ms each. The ‘target value’ was set to 20,000 and dynamic exclusion was activated and set to 0.4 min. The quadrupole isolation width was set to 2 Th for m/z < 700 and 3 Th for m/z > 800.
dataProcessingProtocol: LC-MS/MS raw data was interpreted with MaxQuant 2.2.0.0 software (Cox et al. 2008) using the mouse proteome including isoforms from Uniprot (downloaded: 19.07.2022) as reference data set for protein identification. Proteins were identified with one unique peptide and a false discovery rate (FDR) of 0.01. Search parameters were set as follows: Trypsin/P as digestion enzyme; two missed cleavages were allowed; six amino acids were set as minimum peptide length; oxidation (M), acetyl (protein N-term), and deamidation (NQ) were included as variable modifications. Label free quantification (LFQ) were performed with match between runs enabled using MaxQuant standard settings with an alignment time window of 25 min. MaxQuant results were quality controlled with the PTXQC package (Bielow et al. 2016). MaxQuant results were processed using MSstats (Choi et al. 2014) running on the Galaxy Europe server (usergalaxy.eu; The Galaxy Consortium, 2022). Synaptic protein groups were identified by using SynGo (Koopmans et al. 2019) analysis. For the data analyses the following biological replicates were considered: P15 Pde1c-Cre-/-;DTA (n=6), P15 Pde1c-Cre+/-;DTA (n=4), P30 Pde1c-Cre-/-;DTA (n=2), P30 Pde1c-Cre+/-;DTA (n=7).
